Advisory note - the three questions that prevent most rejections

1. Have you paid anything or signed anything yet?
Gate 0. Accounts for 34.2% of all EDG rejections - the single largest cause.

Is the company name on the quotation the exact ACRA-registered name?
Accounts for 10.5% of rejections. "ABC Global" will be rejected if ACRA says "ABC Global Pte Ltd".

Is the consultant SAC-accredited under TR 43 or SS 680?
EDG management consultancy costs only. Usually discovered too late, at claim stage.

6. What the numbers mean for the Al advisory assistant

The review makes three points that shaped the design of this proof-of-concept assistant.

@ Most failure is preventable, not technical.

Two thirds of rejections trace to four procedural checks that an assistant can ask about in the
first thirty seconds of a conversation. The assistant does not need to be a grants expert to add
value; it needs to be a reliable checklist that never forgets Gate 0.

6 Advisory volume is growing 43% year on year.

Enquiries rose from 246 in Q1 to 351 in Q4. SMF has no in-house technical team and cannot scale
advisory headcount at that rate. Deflecting routine first-line questions is the clearest value case.

6 Wrong numbers are worse than no numbers.

A member who is told the wrong support rate may sign a contract on that basis and lose the whole
grant. The assistant must therefore abstain rather than estimate, and must surface every TO VERIFY

marker in the under! ng advisory notes rather than smoothing it into a confident figure.

Electronics assembly - 215 staff - S$58.4m turnover

PSG NIL - rejected day 19

SITUATION
Wanted PSG support for a warehouse management system.

OUTCOME

Rejected. Group employment size was 215 and group turnover S$58.4m. The member failed the headcount limb of
the SME test and assumed both limbs had to fail.

ADVISORY LESSON

The PSG SME test is group turnover not exceeding S$100m OR group employment not exceeding 200. It is a
single test read as OR, so passing on turnover alone is enough - but this member exceeded 200 staff and
their turnover was under the cap, so they still qualified. The rejection was actually caused by a deposit

paid to the vendor, discovered at review.

What the five journeys have in common.

Case Scheme Gate 0 clean? Correct scheme first time? Outcome

The pattern SMF advisory officers should take away

Two of five cases failed Gate 0, and in both instances the member believed they were still safe -

one because no money had changed hands, the other because the deposit was described by the vendor
as refundable. Neither distinction matters. Any payment, deposit or signed contractual agreement

with a party named in the application constitutes commencement.

One of five cases arrived asking about the wrong scheme entirely. Members frame their need in terms
of the equipment they want to buy, not the policy objective the purchase serves. An energy-efficient
compressor sounds like automation and is actually energy efficiency. Listening for the objective
rather than the object is the core advisory skill this assistant must support.
